title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) that measures whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the fraction of generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical generated candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents using gpt-5-mini and a canonical verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes and 72 model calls. All baseline emulator executions produced no observed faults (contingency n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired reduction in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). We report the preregistered rationale, deterministic execution accounting (planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; model_calls_used = 72; artifact_count = 510), representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and artifact-grounded recommendations for preregistered follow‑on designs that can detect verifier utility when baseline error prevalence is non-negligible.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level network configurations. Intent→configuration automation can accelerate NetOps workflows but risks silently violating reachability, access-control, ordering, or workflow invariants, which can cause outages if generated text is executed without additional checks. A canonical mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture that pairs stochastic generation with deterministic verification and, where permitted, automated repair or human review. Despite architectural proposals and prototypes, systematic preregistered experiments that isolate a verifier's detection performance against executed outcomes using tightly controlled paired designs remain scarce.

We address a narrowly scoped preregistered research question: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and an emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of generated candidates that would execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? This paired estimand isolates verifier detection from generator-side resampling, prompt engineering, or repair-enabled iterations. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) executed end-to-end with archived artifacts, (2) exact deterministic accounting and inferential outputs for the shared_initial_candidate contract, and (3) artifact-grounded diagnostics and concrete preregisterable alternatives that enable non-degenerate inference of verifier utility when baseline error prevalence is nonzero.
sections.related_work: Prior work demonstrates that LLMs can produce device-level configurations from high-level intents in constrained vendor‑dialect settings; these studies show promise but are usually scoped to limited task families and curated datasets rather than diverse production traces [1]. System prototypes and multi-agent/tool‑augmented frameworks illustrate practical integration points for verifiers and domain services in agentic NetOps workflows but commonly evaluate on emulators or curated scenarios rather than preregistered paired detection measurements [2]. In other domains, generate–verify–repair patterns have yielded empirical correctness improvements for code and software repair, highlighting that verification utility depends strongly on baseline generator error rates and on whether the workflow permits verifier-triggered repair or resampling [3]. Canonical deterministic network-verification techniques (e.g., header-space and related reachability/policy analyzers) provide precise semantics-aware invariants for reachability and ACL-style checks and are natural candidates for the verify stage in GVR architectures [4]. The supplied literature therefore motivates our paired detection question while identifying the gap we address: a preregistered paired measurement of verifier detection on identical generated candidates with deterministic execution accounting.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The confirmatory hypothesis targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 with two-sided alpha = 0.05 and power ≥ 0.80; a sample-size heuristic yielded ≈63 pairs and we preregistered N = 72 pairs stratified equally across three difficulty strata.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and experimental contract. Per the frozen contract, for each intent we made exactly one initial LLM generation and evaluated that identical candidate in two paired conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record whether an emulator-observed operational fault occurs. Guarded: run the deterministic verifier on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no executed fault); if it does not flag, execute the identical candidate in the emulator and record the result. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, any observed paired difference can only arise from the verifier preventing execution of a candidate that would otherwise have failed at emulation.

Model and verifier configuration (artifact‑grounded). The declared model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Key recorded model parameters: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", provider = "openai_responses", max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, and temperature = null. We explicitly record that temperature = null indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics (the archived configuration does not set a numeric temperature) rather than an asserted deterministic temperature=0. The canonical verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") running the full_intent_constraint_validation rule set. The verifier emits structured per-episode traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after states, violation_codes, violation_count, difficulty metadata) that form the mechanistic basis for guarded decisions.

Task bank, contamination controls, and stratification. Confirmatory tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task_manifest entry encodes: a natural-language intent, an ordered required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, preserve_unspecified_state policies, initial and expected_final_state snapshots, and a difficulty.level tag (medium/hard/very_hard). Exact-match contamination checks against a public-corpus fingerprint were preregistered; none of the confirmatory pairs were excluded for exact-match contamination. The confirmatory sample followed the preregistered stratification (24 pairs per difficulty stratum).

Execution protocol, retries, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan permitted up to two retries for transient hosted-API errors. The run started and completed on 2026-08-31 within ≈10.1 minutes wall-clock. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 72, and artifact_count = 510. Provider-call audit reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 72 and cache_miss_count = 72. These deterministic accounting artifacts confirm one shared generation per pair and no cross-condition additional generation activity.

Scoring and inferential procedures. For each episode the verifier produced a binary validity verdict and a validator_trace JSON. The scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation (verifier enforces required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and preserve_unspecified_state). The primary analysis used a registered paired_binary_analysis executor to construct the 2×2 contingency table (guarded × baseline) where an undetected executed fault is 1. The prespecified inferential test is exact McNemar when discordant pairs exist; we also computed paired bootstrap-percentile 95% confidence intervals with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Pre-registered subgroup confirmatory comparisons and Holm correction were implemented but are non-informative in the absence of discordant pairs. All analysis steps were executed by deterministic scripts and archived.
sections.results:
Execution summary and manifest figures. The autonomous pipeline completed without technical failures. Key manifest figures: planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 72; artifact_count = 510. analysis/condition_summary reports baseline successes = 72, baseline failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 72, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0).

Paired contingency and inferential output. Aggregating across the 72 confirmatory pairs produced contingency counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) is [0.0, 0.0]. These values are archived and derive directly from the preregistered estimand and observed data.

Representative validator diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts show consistent verifier behavior on shared candidates: parsed_command_count equals required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for representative tasks across difficulty strata. Example summarised traces (artifact-grounded): pair-000001 (medium): parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, violation_count = 0; pair-000002 (hard): parsed_command_count = 2, required_command_count = 2, violation_count = 0; pair-000003 (hard): parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, violation_count = 0. These traces explain why no verifier flags occurred and why baseline emulator executions also observed no faults for the sampled tasks.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the degenerate confirmatory outcome. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate design cleanly isolates verifier detection on identical candidates. When the identical generated candidates produce no emulator-observed faults the paired difference must algebraically be zero; the verifier cannot reduce executed faults that do not occur. The observed contingency (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0) and exact inferential outputs (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]) are therefore an expected and artifact-grounded consequence of the contract and the recorded generation/verifier alignment.

Artifact-grounded attribution. Archived artifacts allow concrete attribution of the ceiling outcome to measurable pipeline factors: (i) the deterministic task generator encoded explicit required_sequence and allowed_touched_fields that narrow acceptable candidates; (ii) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced candidates that matched those constraints across the synthetic corpus (shared_initial_candidate traces); and (iii) the verifier enforced the same manifest constraints (full_intent_constraint_validation), producing parsed_command_count = required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for representative episodes. This alignment explains the absence of baseline emulator faults in our confirmatory set.

Implications for confirmatory design and power. A paired confirmatory test targeting an absolute reduction (e.g., 0.20) requires a non‑zero baseline prevalence of executed faults to have power. When baseline prevalence is zero the paired difference must be zero regardless of verifier capability. To measure verifier utility in practice, preregistered designs must ensure measurable baseline error prevalence (for example, via adversarial seeding) or must permit verification to influence candidate distributions (independent-generation or repair-enabled arms).

Concrete, preregisterable alternatives. The archived pipeline supports several preregisterable modifications that would enable non-degenerate inference without inventing new artifacts here: (1) independent-generation arm: allow separate initial generator calls per condition so verifier-triggered repair or resampling can change candidate distributions and produce discordant pairs; (2) repair-enabled flow: permit one deterministic repair attempt when the verifier flags violations and execute the repaired candidate to measure end-to-end improvement; (3) adversarial/fault-injection task bank: seed intents with ambiguous wording, ordering subtleties, or vendor-edge cases to raise baseline error prevalence; (4) sampling-parameter sweeps and multi-model comparisons: set explicit non-null temperature and test multiple model versions to quantify model- and sampling-sensitivity; and (5) false-positive cost arms: quantify operational blocking cost by measuring flagged-but-safe candidates and repair/delay outcomes. These alternatives are preregisterable and implementable using the same deterministic execution and analysis infrastructure archived with this run (the analysis scripts executed the bootstrap diagnostics with seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples as recorded). Implementing any alternative requires adjusting the preregistered estimand and accounting rules accordingly.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates verifier detection but precludes verifier-mediated resampling or repair effects; deterministic provider-call audits confirm the isolation. Construct validity: emulator-executed faults are a conservative surrogate for operational harm but omit traffic-dependent timing and vendor-hardware idiosyncrasies. External validity: the experiment used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic task bank; extrapolation to other models or production traces is limited. Conclusion validity: with zero baseline faults the preregistered power targets are inapplicable; future confirmatory designs should align expected baseline prevalence with power calculations.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to test whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires preregistered contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. The archived artifacts and deterministic accounting provide a reproducible template for those follow‑on confirmatory designs and power calculations.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and approved the immutable initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Models and orchestration: initial generation used gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in the archived model configuration) orchestrated via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") served as the canonical verifier; an isolated emulator executed candidate configurations. Preregistration: study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 was preregistered and frozen before observing outcomes. Immutable master-prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Key archived artifacts (execution and analysis manifests, per-episode validator traces, and raw responses) are recorded and available for audit with the archived run. Note: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null, which indicates provider-default sampling semantics in the archived configuration rather than an asserted numeric temperature value.
limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: the baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit under the shared_initial_candidate contract.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per-condition generation, multi-sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single-model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: the task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling-parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (provider-default sampling semantics archived); this is an archived configuration uncertainty rather than an explicitly controlled numeric temperature.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact-match checks were applied, but private training-data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
